subject.title: [Feature]: Structured Callback Actions and Thread Context Inheritance for Agent Handoffs

question: Should OpenClaw extend `sessions_send` with a structured skip/no-reply/announce routing API, and what exact compatibility shape should own that contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding `action`, announce routing overrides, or dispatch/no-reply modes changes the model-facing tool contract and overlaps with several open A2A product requests.

options.title: Approve a single typed handoff contract
options.body: Fold structured skip/no-reply outcome, announce target selection, and thread inheritance into one reviewed `sessions_send`/handoff API with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Narrow this to acceptance coverage only
options.body: Keep this issue open as tests and requirements for a future handoff protocol while implementation proceeds through a separate canonical design item.

options.title: Reject new core API for now
options.body: Keep exact-token behavior plus existing thread fixes and close or redirect the remaining structured-action request if maintainers do not want more A2A core surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a single typed handoff contract
recommendation.body: Fold structured skip/no-reply outcome, announce target selection, and thread inheritance into one reviewed `sessions_send`/handoff API with focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He already provided the item-specific routing comment and has recent adjacent sessions/A2A history, making him the best available product-decision owner from the inspected trail.
